Although the concept is sound, the analogy isn't, because the assumption is that a VPN is a defense, when it is instead voluntary data sifting.

In short, when you use a VPN, you divide up your browsing. If you kept the same relative activity levels on either, then the concept would be valid from a security standpoint, but because you concentrate your most valuable internet activity (the activity any snoop is most interested in) into one stream (leaving another stream which, can be reasoned, must have lesser value), you enable them to safely reason certain things, like:

1) Monitoring of your ISP traffic is now unnecessary, saving their resources, in favor of monitoring the concentrated stream at your VPN operator 2) The very act of using a VPN, along with your previous clearnet browsing history, can be used as justification alone for CALEA interdiction, much less any legal justification needed - if needed at all - to gain access to your VPN log or realtime bitstream.

  1. Relative costs of defense vs costs to break, and
  2. Lack of 'herd immunity'

Considering the second point first, if there isn't some critical mass of people with nearly all of their traffic moved to VPNs, then it is similarly easy to concentrate resources on those who do. Lab tech here. I’ve seen many cases of this. Usually the triglycerides are so high you have to use an airfuge, a special type of centrifuge that separates out the triglycerides from the rest of the serum so that you can get valid readings on other chemistries. Particularly the liver enzymes. Triglycerides really interfere with the assay at this high of a level. Usually their triglycerides are above 1500 mg/dL. For reference, normal should be below 150.

Airfuging is kind of cool. You really do end up with something that has the look and consistency of butter on top with clear serum underneath. Usually it’s not fatties, but people with genetic lipid disorders. Fatties usually sit more in the 200-400 range, non-fasting.
